+        for mainpos, sideturn in zip(self.main_positions, self._side_chain_turns):
+            if sideturn is None:
+                side_positions.append(None)
+            else:

+            counter += 1

+        """
+        side_positions: List[Optional[np.ndarray]] = []
+        counter = 1
+        for mainpos, sideturn in zip(self.main_positions, self._side_chain_turns):
+            if sideturn is None:
+                side_positions.append(None)
+            else:
+                side_positions.append(mainpos + (-1) ** counter * self.COORDINATES[sideturn])

+            counter += 1

body:
I agree with Steve's previous comment, that you should be using `tempfile` to determine the location where this file goes.
This will also prevent leaving around left-over files, in case the test below fails (in which case the `os.remove` call would never happen).

See here for an existing example: https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-nature/blob/cf61e81473c97b5f7b290e24a02ade2c1b08a9ac/test/drivers/second_quantization/fcidumpd/test_driver_fcidump_dumper.py#L132

The thing is that the plot can be rotated with the mouse by the user if we turn on the interactive plot. Max was saying that that uses too much javascript and that we are better off with plain graphics. However I explain in the notebook that the option can be turned on if rendered properly. I also added a manual rotation so that even if we are in 2D it doesn't look as bad.
``` python
fig = result.get_figure(title="Protein Structure", ticks=True, grid=True)
fig.get_axes()[0].view_init(10,70)
fig.show()
```
Regarding the different shades of blue. This is just how matplotlib renders objects that are closer or further away. It allows to percieve some depth and I don't think we should turn it off.
